Look up almost anywhere, and sooner or later a bird will cross the sky. There are birds in the coldest ice and the hottest desert, in the deepest forest and the busiest city. There are birds smaller than your thumb, and birds taller than a grown man. This is the story of the feathered creatures who share our world, and rule its skies.

image.note: Many kinds of birds against the sky

pages.text: Birds come in a dazzling variety, in every colour and size you can imagine. Yet every single one, from the tiniest to the tallest, shares the same handful of special features, features that no other animal has, and that make a bird a bird.

image.note: A colourful variety of birds together

pages.text: What makes a bird a bird? Not simply that it flies, for some birds cannot, and some other animals can. A bird is an animal with feathers, with a beak and no teeth, with two wings, and which lays eggs. Feathers, above all, are the true mark of a bird. No other animal on earth has them.

image.note: The features of a bird labelled: feathers, beak, wings

pages.text: There are birds to suit almost every way of living. Tiny birds that sip from flowers, great birds that soar for hours without a wingbeat, swimming birds that fly underwater, running birds that never leave the ground. Whatever the place, some clever bird has found a way to make its living there.

Most birds can do something we never can without machines: they fly. And their whole bodies are built for it. Their bones are not solid like ours, but hollow and light, filled with air, so a bird is far lighter than it looks. A skeleton that would weigh you down would let a bird float up.

Their wings are shaped with wonderful cleverness, curved just so, so that air flows faster over the top than beneath, and lifts the bird up as it moves forward. Powerful chest muscles beat the wings, and a bird can climb, dive, hover, and turn, master of the open air.

image.note: A bird's wing shape lifting it into the air

pages.text: Not all birds fly, though. The ostrich is far too heavy, but it runs faster than a racehorse on its long, strong legs. The penguin cannot fly through air, but it flies through water instead, its wings become flippers. Each has traded the sky for something else it needed more.

image.note: An ostrich running and a penguin swimming

pages.text: Feathers are a wonder all their own. They are light, and strong, and do many jobs at once. The long, stiff feathers of the wings and tail push against the air for flight. The soft, fluffy feathers beneath keep the bird warm, trapping heat like the cosiest coat.

image.note: Different kinds of feathers: flight and down

pages.text: Feathers are for showing off, too. Many birds wear brilliant colours, to dazzle a mate or warn off a rival. The peacock spreads a fan of shimmering eyes; the tiny hummingbird flashes like a jewel. And some birds wear dull colours instead, the better to hide, unseen, from anything that might eat them.

image.note: A dazzling peacock beside a well-hidden bird

pages.text: Every bird begins as an egg. Unlike you, birds do not grow their young inside them, for that would make them too heavy to fly. Instead the mother lays eggs, in a snug nest, and the parents keep them warm until, at last, the chicks peck their way out into the world.

image.note: Eggs in a nest, a chick hatching

pages.text: Birds build the most marvellous nests, each kind in its own way, with no one to teach them. Some weave baskets of grass that hang from branches. Some glue tiny cups to walls. Some dig burrows, or pile great platforms of sticks. And they build them knowing exactly how, born with the skill inside them.

image.note: A variety of amazing bird nests

pages.text: Some birds make journeys so astonishing they are hard to believe. As the seasons turn and their home grows cold or bare, they fly away, thousands of miles, to warmer lands, and back again when the season changes. This great voyage is called migration.

image.note: Flocks of birds migrating across the world

pages.text: One small bird flies from the very top of the world to the very bottom and back again each year, further than any other animal travels, chasing an endless summer. How they find their way, over oceans, with no map and no guide, is one of the great mysteries of nature. Somehow, they simply know.

image.note: A small bird flying pole to pole across the globe

pages.text: Birds live in every land on earth, and share our towns and gardens too. Listen in the early morning, and you will hear them: a great chorus of songs and calls, birds speaking to one another across the rooftops, as they have every dawn since long before there were any people to listen.

image.note: Birds singing in a town at dawn

pages.text: So the next time a bird crosses your sky, look, and think of the wonder of it: hollow bones and clever wings, a coat of feathers found on no other animal, a nest built by instinct, and perhaps a journey of thousands of miles behind it. The commonest bird in your garden is a small miracle of the air.

image.note: A child watching a common bird with new wonder

pages.text: Words to know. Feathers: the special covering only birds have. Beak: a bird's mouth, with no teeth. Migration: the long seasonal journey some birds make. Hollow bones: light bones that help birds fly. Nest: the home a bird builds for its eggs.
Birds rule the sky, but the world teems with other creatures too, crawling, buzzing, and creeping. Some of the most amazing of all are also the smallest. Which will you discover next?
